public_rationale: The candidate announcement was considered, but it does not establish the AGI antecedent or settle the architectural prediction. With the condition unknown, the conditional-forecast rule prevents scoring. The announcement is a reason to investigate possible arrival, not counterevidence proving that an explicit type/token distinction is unnecessary.
limitations: Broad acceptance and the operational meaning of explicit are evaluator interpretations.
Failure to locate a disclosed mechanism does not prove it is absent.
A token vocabulary or successful classification behavior would not by itself establish the claimed distinction.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Whenever AGI arrives, an explicit type/token distinction will be crucial to it.

statement.excerpt: 👉an explicit type/token distinction will be crucial
statement.document_title: Does AI really need a paradigm shift?

from_speaker: tied not to time but to architecture
our_interpretation: Treat arrival as a demonstrated system with broadly accepted human-level general cognitive capability. Broad acceptance is an evaluator safeguard.
Read type/token distinction as an explicit separation between a general kind or category and particular instances of it.
Language-model tokenization alone does not establish this distinction in the system's reasoning.
Read crucial as central dependence supported by component tests or equivalent evidence.
Test the first broadly accepted AGI; dependence in that system would support the arrival prediction without proving universal necessity.
criteria.support_condition: The AGI condition is established, and technical evidence shows an explicit kind-versus-instance representation whose removal substantially undermines the arriving system's general capability.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The AGI condition is established, and complete architectural evidence or controlled tests show that the system achieves general capability without an explicit type/token distinction.
